verses.zh: 我说：雅各的首领，以色列家的官长啊，你们要听！你们不当知道公平吗？
verses.en: I said,“Listen, you leaders[NOTE:1] of Jacob,you rulers of the nation[NOTE:2] of Israel!You ought to know what is just,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “heads.”
Heb “house.”
Heb “Should you not know justice?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course you should!”

verses.zh: 你们恶善好恶，从人身上剥皮，从人骨头上剔肉，
verses.en: yet you[NOTE:1] hate what is good[NOTE:2] and love what is evil.[NOTE:3] You flay my people’s skin[NOTE:4] and rip the flesh from their bones.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “the ones who.”
Or “good.”
Or “evil.”

Heb “their skin from upon them.” The referent of the pronoun (“my people,” referring to Jacob and/or the house of Israel, with the Lord as the speaker) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and their flesh from their bones.”sn Micah compares the social injustice perpetrated by the house of Jacob/Israel to cannibalism because it threatens the very lives of the oppressed.

verses.zh: 吃我民的肉，剥他们的皮，打折他们的骨头，分成块子像要下锅，又像釜中的肉。
verses.en: You[NOTE:1] devour my people’s flesh,strip off their skin,and crush their bones.You chop them up like flesh in a pot[NOTE:2]—like meat in a kettle.
notes: Heb “who.”
The MT reads “and they chop up as in a pot.” The translation assumes an emendation of כַּאֲשֶׁר (ka’asher, “as”) to כִּשְׁאֵר (kishʾer, “like flesh”).

verses.zh: 到了遭灾的时候，这些人必哀求耶和华，他却不应允他们。那时他必照他们所行的恶事向他们掩面。
verses.en: Someday these sinful leaders[NOTE:1] will cry to the Lord for help,but he will not answer them.He will hide his face from them at that time,because they have done such wicked deeds.”
notes: Heb “they,” referring to the indicted leaders in vv. 1-3.

verses.zh: 论到使我民走差路的先知―他们牙齿有所嚼的，他们就呼喊说：平安了！凡不供给他们吃的，他们就预备攻击他（预备攻击他：或译说必遭遇刀兵）―耶和华如此说：
verses.en: This is what the Lord has said about the prophets who mislead my people,[NOTE:1] “If someone gives them enough to eat,they offer an oracle of peace.[NOTE:2] But if someone does not give them food,they are ready to declare war on him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “concerning the prophets, those who mislead my people.” Some prefer to begin the quotation after “the Lord has said” (cf. NIV). But when the preposition עַל (ʿal, “about”) occurs with this introductory formula it regularly indicates who is being spoken about. (When a person is not the object of the preposition, it may begin the quote, meaning “because.”) Including the first person pronominal suffix (in “my people”) after a third person introduction may sound awkward, but also occurs in Jer 14:15; 23:2 (and perhaps Jer 12:14, a text critical question). Hillers prefers to add הוֹי (hoy, “woe, ah”) at the beginning of the quotation, after the graphically similar יְהוָה (yehvah; see D. R. Hillers, Micah [Hermeneia], 44). The phrase הוֹי עַל (hoy ʿal, “woe upon”) occurs in Jer 50:27 and Ezek 13:3 (with “the prophets” following the preposition in the latter instance).

Heb “those who bite with their teeth and cry out, ‘peace.’” The phrase “bite with the teeth” is taken here as idiomatic for eating. Apparently these prophets were driven by mercenary motives. If they were paid well, they gave positive oracles to their clients, but if someone could not afford to pay them, they were hostile and delivered oracles of doom.
Heb “but [as for the one] who does not place [food] in their mouths, they prepare for war against him.”

verses.zh: 你们必遭遇黑夜，以致不见异象；又必遭遇幽暗，以致不能占卜。日头必向你们沉落，白昼变为黑暗。
verses.en: Therefore night will fall, and you will receive no visions;[NOTE:1] it will grow dark, and you will no longer be able to read the omens.[NOTE:2] The sun will set on these prophets,and the daylight will turn to darkness over their heads.[NOTE:3]
notes: The coming of night (and darkness in the following line) symbolizes the cessation of revelation.tn Heb “it will be night for you without a vision.”

The reading of omens (Heb “divination”) was forbidden in the law (Deut 18:10), so this probably reflects the prophets’ view of how they received divine revelation.tn Heb “it will be dark for you without divination.”
Heb “and the day will be dark over them.”

verses.zh: 先见必抱愧，占卜的必蒙羞，都必捂着嘴唇，因为　神不应允他们。
verses.en: The prophets[NOTE:1] will be ashamed;the omen readers will be humiliated.All of them will cover their mouths,[NOTE:2] for they will receive no divine oracles.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “seers.”
Or “the mustache,” or perhaps “the beard.” Cf. KJV, NAB, NRSV “cover their lips.”
Heb “no divine response” or “no answer from God.”

verses.zh: 至于我，我藉耶和华的灵，满有力量、公平、才能，可以向雅各说明他的过犯，向以色列指出他的罪恶。
verses.en: But I[NOTE:1] am full of the courage that the Lord’s Spirit givesand have a strong commitment to justice.[NOTE:2] This enables me to confront Jacob with its rebellionand Israel with its sin.[NOTE:3]
notes: The prophet Micah speaks here and contrasts himself with the mercenaries just denounced by the Lord in the preceding verses.

Heb “am full of power, the Spirit of the Lord, and justice and strength.” The appositional phrase “the Spirit of the Lord” explains the source of the prophet’s power. The phrase “justice and strength” is understood here as a hendiadys, referring to the prophet’s strong sense of justice.
Heb “to declare to Jacob his rebellion and to Israel his sin.” The words “this enables me” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 雅各家的首领、以色列家的官长啊，当听我的话！你们厌恶公平，在一切事上屈枉正直；
verses.en: Listen to this, you leaders of the family[NOTE:1] of Jacob,you rulers of the nation[NOTE:2] of Israel!You[NOTE:3] hate justiceand pervert all that is right.
notes: Heb “house.”
Heb “house.”
Heb “who.” A new sentence was begun here in the translation for stylistic reasons (also at the beginning of v. 10).

verses.zh: 以人血建立锡安，以罪孽建造耶路撒冷。
verses.en: You[NOTE:1] build Zion through bloody crimes,[NOTE:2] Jerusalem[NOTE:3] through unjust violence.
notes: Heb “who.”
Heb “bloodshed” (so NAB, NASB, NIV); NLT “murder.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 首领为贿赂行审判；祭司为雇价施训诲；先知为银钱行占卜。他们却倚赖耶和华，说：耶和华不是在我们中间吗？灾祸必不临到我们。
verses.en: Her[NOTE:1] leaders take bribes when they decide legal cases,[NOTE:2] her priests proclaim rulings for profit,and her prophets read omens for pay.Yet they claim to trust[NOTE:3] the Lord and say,“The Lord is among us.[NOTE:4] Disaster will not overtake[NOTE:5] us!”
notes: The pronoun Her refers to Jerusalem (note the previous line).
Heb “judge for a bribe.”
Heb “they lean upon” (so KJV, NIV84, NRSV); NAB “rely on”; NIV11 “look for support.”
Heb “Is not the Lord in our midst?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course he is!”
Or “come upon” (so many English versions); NCV “happen to us”; CEV “come to us.”

verses.zh: 所以因你们的缘故，锡安必被耕种像一块田，耶路撒冷必变为乱堆；这殿的山必像丛林的高处。
verses.en: Therefore, because of you,[NOTE:1] Zion will be plowed up like[NOTE:2] a field,Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins,and the Temple Mount[NOTE:3] will become a hill overgrown with brush![NOTE:4]
notes: The plural pronoun refers to the leaders, priests, and prophets mentioned in the preceding verse.
Or “into” (an adverbial accusative of result).
Heb “the mountain of the house” (so KJV, ASV, NRSV).
Heb “a high place of overgrowth.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BRIEF OUTLINE OF THE CHAPTER ‒ YHWH calls the evil leaders of Judah to account.

- Political rulers, Micah 3:1-4

- Prophets, Micah 3:5-8

- false prophets described in Micah 3:5-7

- true prophets described in Micah 3:8

- Civil rulers, priests, and prophets are addressed collectively, Micah 3:9-12

- There is an obvious parallelism between A. and C. (i.e. "hear," shema, Qal IMPERATIVE; see
Special Topic: Listen/Hear (shema))

- See full outline in Introduction VII.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: MICAH 3:1-4

1"And I said,

'Hear now, heads of Jacob

And rulers of the house of Israel.

Is it not for you to know justice?

2You who hate good and love evil,

Who tear off their skin from them

And their flesh from their bones,

3And who eat the flesh of my people,

Strip off their skin from them,

Break their bones,

And chop them up as for the pot

And as meat in a kettle."

4Then they will cry out to the Lord,

But He will not answer them.

Instead, He will hide His face from them at that time,

Because they have practiced evil deeds.

3:1 This is a strong contrast to Micah 2:12-13. The abrupt transition from judgment to restoration characterizes this book. This literary technique
may be unconsciously related to the antithetical parallelism of Hebrew poetry! Chapter 3 picks up again on the theme of Divine judgment from Micah 2.

Special Topic: Hebrew Poetry

▣ "Hear" This is the Hebrew Shema (BDB 1033, KB 1570,
Qal IMPERATIVE), which means to hear so as to do
(cf. Micah 1:2; 3:1; 6:1). This word seems to outline the book. See note at Micah 1:2.

Special Topic: Listen/Hear (shema)

▣ ". . .heads of Jacob

And rulers of the house of Israel.

Is it not for you to know justice" All three lines of poetry refer to the political leaders of Judah (cf. Micah 3:9-10) who should have
been trained in the Mosaic law (cf. Deut. 12:17), but followed a policy of greed and self-centeredness (cf. Amos 5:15; Isa. 1:16,17). Calling Judah, Israel, probably shows

- this was spoken after the fall of the Northern Ten Tribes to Assyria in 722 B.C.

- it was a way of showing condemnation (e.g. Ezekiel 23)

- Israel was the colletive term for all the tribes before the split in 922 B.C.

Special Topic: Israel (the name)

▣ "justice" See Special Topic: Justice

3:2-3 Instead of acting like shepherds, these political leaders (cf. Ezekiel 34) acted like butchers (i.e. "tear off," "strip off," "break," "chop").

- "tear off" ‒ BDB 159, KB 186, Qal PARTICIPLE, cf. Micah 2:8; 7:2,3

- "strip off" ‒ BDB 832, KB 980, Hiphil PERFECT, cf. Ezek. 34:2,3

- "break" ‒ BDB822, KB 953, Piel PERFECT

- "chop: ‒ BDB 831, KB 975, Qal PERFECT, cf. Ezek. 11:3,6,7

The phrase, "eat the flesh of my people," is used in a figurative sense in Ps. 14:4, 27:2 and Prov. 30:14.

3:2 "You who hate good and love evil" The two VERBS "hate" (BDB 971, KB 1338) and "love" (BDB 12, KB 17)
are both Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLES. These leaders' response was exactly opposite from YHWH's will (cf. Isa. 1:16-17, 21-23,
26; 5:7,8,20; Amos 5:15; note Jesus' words in Matt. 6:23).

3:4 "Then they will cry out to the Lord,

But He will not answer them" The VERB
"cry out" (BDB 227, KB 277, Qal IMPERFECT) is a legal term
for appealing to the court for help.

- as these wicked judges did not hear the cries of the poor aliens, orphans, and widows

- God will not hear their cry either (cf.Deut. 31:17,18; 32:20; Prov. 21:13; Isa. 1:15; 59:2; 64:7;
Jer. 33:5; James 2:13)

▣ "He will hide His face from them at that time" The VERB (BDB 711, KB 771, Hiphil) is JUSSIVE
in form, but not in meaning.

The "them" refers to the faithless leaders. This is ultimate rejection.

- "He will not answer them," v. 4

- "He will hide His face from them" (cf. Deut. 31:17; Isa. 1:15)

- The Aramaic Targums translate this as YHWH remembering His shekinah glory

Special Topic: Shekinah

▣ "Because they have practiced evil deeds" Here is the problem. YHWH's people have repeatedly and flagrantly rebelled and
rejected their covenant obligations (cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 28). They are now reaping what they sowed (cf. Micah 7:13; Isa. 3:10,11; see full list of
Scripture parallels at Gal. 6:7-10).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: MICAH 3:5-12

5" Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets

Who lead my people astray;

When they have something to bite with their teeth,

They cry, "Peace,"

But against him who puts nothing in their mouths,

They declare holy war.

6Therefore it will be night for you-without vision,

And darkness for you-without divination.

The sun will go down on the prophets,

And the day will become dark over them.

7The seers will be ashamed

And the diviners will be embarrassed.

Indeed, they will all cover their mouths

Because there is no answer from God.

8On the other hand I am filled with power-

With the Spirit of the Lord-

And with justice and courage

To make known to Jacob his rebellious act,

Even to Israel his sin.

9Now hear this, heads of the house of Jacob

And rulers of the house of Israel,

Who abhor justice

And twist everything that is straight,

10Who build Zion with bloodshed

And Jerusalem with violent injustice.

11Her leaders pronounce judgment for a bribe,

Her priests instruct for a price,

And her prophets divine for money.

Yet they lean on the Lord saying,

'Is not the Lord in our midst?

Calamity will not come upon us.'

12Therefore, on account of you,

Zion will be plowed as a field,

Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins,

And the mountain of the temple will become high places of a forest."

3:5 "Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets" The prophets were one of several ways to know
the will of YHWH. The very ones who were to reveal YHWH, did not know Him (cf. Hosea 4:1). 1 Sam. 28:6 mentions three ways Saul inquired of YHWH:

- dreams, visions

- Urim and Thummim (i.e. High Priest)

- prophet (i.e. Samuel)

Special Topic: Names for Deity, D.

Special Topic: Ways of Revelation

Special Topic: Prophecy (OT), I. B. #3

▣ "Who lead my people astray" The VERB (BDB 1073, KB 1766, Hiphil PARTICIPLE)
means "to cause to err" (cf. Amos 2:4; Hosea 4:12; 2 Kgs. 21:9; Isa. 3:12; 9:16; Jer. 50:6). This refers to the false prophets mentioned in Micah 2:6-7; 3:10-11.

▣ "When they have something to bite with their teeth" This refers to the eating of food (i.e. gifts from the people they prophesied
for, cf. Micah 3:5, lines 4 and 5). They prophesy for hire, not for God (cf. Isa. 59:9-11). They tell

- the generous clients just what they want to hear (i.e. peace and prosperity)

- their poor clients problems and scarcity

The term "bite" (BDB 675, KB 729, Qal PARTICIPLE) usually refers to a snake bite.

▣ "They cry, 'Peace'" Literally shalom (BDB 1022) is the Hebrew word which means "wholeness." Apparently,

- if the prophets were well-fed (i.e. paid in food, cf. 1 Sam. 9:7-8), they would
proclaim good news (e.g. Jer. 5:12; 6:13-14; 8:10-11; 13:14; 23:17; Ezek. 13:10)

- if they were not well-fed, they would proclaim "holy war" (BDB 536)

Their message was based on selfish interests, not YHWH's will. These prophets were available for private, as well as, royal consultations.

However, giving a gift to a prophet was a common practice (e.g. 1 Kgs. 14:3; 2 Kgs. 4:42; 8:8-9). It is the manipulation of the message that is the problem!

Special Topic: Peace (OT, shalom)

▣ "They declare holy war" The term "holy" is not in the MT, but comes from the VERB (BDB 872, KB 1073, Piel
PERFECT with waw), which comes from the Hebrew root for "holy." It is used to describe setting apart certain people for war in Jer. 51:27;
Joel 3:9 and here (cf. Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the Old Testament, p. 177).

The implication is that God will send bad things, problems, conflicts against those who are not generous with the prophets
(i.e. YHWH's spokesperson). I sense this same technique today in tithing sermons that pronounce doom if you do not give a set percentage to the
speaker or church (i.e. storehouse tithing)!

Special Topic: Tithing

3:6 "night. . .darkness. . .sun will go down. . .day will become dark" These are four terrible images (no sunlight used by Isaiah) for the removal
of God's Spirit and insight from the rulers and prophets.

Darkness is used as imagery for lack of revelation (i.e. light, e.g. Ps. 82:5; Prov. 2:13; 4:19; Isa. 59:9; 2 Pet. 1:19; 1 John 1:6; 2:11). The
darkness will result in judgment (cf. Amos 5:18-20; another similar image in Amos 8:11-12 is famine of God's word).

YHWH will not respond to

- their prayers

- their prophets

Special Topic: Darkness, I.

▣ "vision" Visions (BDB 302) and dreams (BDB 321) were often paralleled (cf. Job 33:15; Isa. 29:7; Dan. 7:1) as ways of receiving
YHWH's message. Usually (but not exclusively) visions occurred in the day and dreams at night.

Special Topic: Ways of Revelation

▣ "divination" This (BDB 890, KB 1115) was an ancient means of knowing and effecting the future through some physical or mechanical
means (e.g. negative, Deut. 18:9-22; positive, 1 Sam. 28:6 and Gen. 44:5,15). Divination is mankind's attempt to conrol their own lives instead of trusting YHWH.

Special Topic: Divination

3:7 "seers" This was the earliest name for prophets (BDB 302, e.g. 1 Sam. 9:9; 2 Sam. 24:11; 1 Chr. 9:22; 25:5; Isa. 30:10; Amos 7:12).

Special Topic: Prophecy (OT), I. B.

The VERB (BDB 101, KB 116, Qal PERFECT with waw) means to be ashamed

▣ "Because there is no answer from God" These leaders are suffering the same lack of communication with God as the leaders
described in Micah 3:4 (cf. 1 Sam. 28:6). Heaven is silent!

3:8 As verses 5-7 have been a discussion of false (LXX) prophets (cf. Amos 8:11-12), Micah 3:8 is a description of a true prophet who is in
full communication with YHWH (cf. Ps. 89:13-14, the true prophet shares, or better reflects, the character of God).

Notice the true prophet is filled (BDB 569, KB 583,
Qal PERFECT) with

- power (BDB 470)

- YHWH's Spirit (cf. Isa. 11:2; Ezek. 2:2)

- justice (BDB 1048 "judgment")

- courage (BDB 150 "might") to make sin known (cf. Isa. 58:1)

What a contrast with the leaders' shame, grief, and impotence!

Although the full doctrine of the indwelling Holy Spirit,
the third person of the Trinity, is not obvious in the OT, the personal presence
of God with and within humans is revealed:

- Bezalel, Exod. 31:3; 35:31

- Joshua, Deut. 34:9

- Saul, 1 Sam. 19:23-24

- Elijah, 1 Kgs. 18:46

- Ezekiel, Ezek. 1:3; 37:1; 40:1

- Micah, Micah 3:8

- Messiah, Isaiah 11:2; 48:16; 61:1 (Luke 4:18-19)

As evil indwells humans, so too, the personal presence of YHWH. Fallen humans are directed and/or influenced by one of two spiritual forces.

Special Topic: Spirit in the Bible

Special Topic: The Personhood of the Spirit

Special Topic: The Trinity

▣

NASB

NKJV, Peshitta
"but truly"

NRSV, TEV
"but as for me"

Literally the MT has "but indeed I." The Hebrew ADVERB (BDB 19) is a strong ADVERSATIVE
(used often in Job, cf. Micah 1:11; 11:5; 12:7; 13:4; 14:18; 17:10; 33:1).

▣ "Jacob. . .Israel" As the last two lines of Micah 3:8 show Micah addressing both Judah's sins and Israel's sins, so too, lines 1 and 2
of Micah 3:9. It is often difficult to know if Micah is addressing Israel, Judah, or both by these two collective names.

Special Topic: Israel (the name)

3:9

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta
"Now hear this"

NRSV, JPSOA
"hear this"

TEV
"listen to me"

NJB
"kindly listen to this"

REB
"Listen to this"

LXX
"Do hear this"

This phrase is literally "hear I pray this."

- The VERB (BDB 1033, KB 1570) is a Qal IMPERATIVE

- followed by a PARTICLE used for entreaty (בא)

- the DEMONSTRATIVE ADJECTIVE "this"

▣ "Who abhor justice" The VERB (BDB 1073, KB 1765, Piel PARTICIPLE)
means regard as an abomination (e.g. Amos 5:10; 6:8; Isa. 14:19; 49:7). These leaders were not sincerely wrong, but haters of the right,
good, and godly (cf. Isa. 5:20; Amos 6:12).

The term "justice" (BDB 1048) is repeated in Micah 3:8 and 9.

Special Topic: Justice

▣ "And twist everything that is straight" The VERB "twist" (BDB 786, KB 875, Piel IMPERFECT)
means "to pervert" or "to make crooked" (cf. Prov. 10:9; 28:18; Isa. 59:8).

The term "straight" is the etymological root of the OT term for "justice" or "righteousness," which meant a straight edge or measuring
reed (cf. Isa. 5:20). Most of the Hebrew words for sin speak of a deviation from this Divine standard.

Special Topic: Righteousness

3:10 "Zion. . .Jerusalem" Zion is the name of one of the seven hills upon which Jerusalem was built. It often is used to refer to the
whole city or nation. This must be Judah.

Special Topic: Zion

▣ "with bloodshed. . .with violent injustice" These two NOUNS are parallel (cf. Jer. 22:13,17; Hab. 2:12).

3:11 All three groups of leaders are mentioned in this verse and all three are condemned for their greedy, materialistic attitude
(cf. Micah 7:3; Isa. 56:9-12; Jer. 5:30-31; 6:13-14; 8:8-12; 14:13-18,22-23; 26:10-15,16; Ezek. 13; 22:23-31).

▣ "pronounce judgment for a bribe" This shows the corruption of the judiciary (cf. Micah 7:3; 2 Chr. 19:7; Isa. 1:23; 5:23). Wealth
controlled every aspect of the covenant peoples' life.

Special Topic: Wealth

▣ "priests instruct for a price" One role of the priests (and Levites) was to educate the people on the precepts of the Mosaic
Law (e.g. Deut. 33:10; 2 Chr. 15:3; 17:9). Priestly understanding and teaching (and living) of the Mosaic Law was crucial to a healthy, spiritual Israel
(cf. Hosea 4:6). But, here they educate only for a price (cf. Micah 3:5).

Special Topic: Levitical Priests

▣ "Yet they lean on the Lord, saying" The term "lean" is used of leaning on a staff (BDB 1043, KB 1612,
Niphal IMPERFECT, cf. Ps. 23:4). These leaders were wrapping their evil deeds in religious dress. Their mouth said one thing; their
actions another (cf. Isa. 29:13)! They were claiming YHWH's protection (covenant benefit) because of their covenant relationship to Him, but were completely
ignoring the covenant requirements (cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 27-29; Isa. 6:9-10; 29:13). The Mosaic Covenant was conditional!

▣ "Calamity will not come upon us" This must have been a recurrent theme of the false prophets, which became a cultural
proverb (cf. Jer. 5:12; 23:17; Amos 9:10), but they were wrong (cf. Micah 2:3).

3:12 This must have been an extremely startling statement to the people of Judah. They trusted in YHWH's promises that Jerusalem and the
temple would never fall (i.e. Isaiah's promises to Hezekiah, probably based in 2 Samuel 7), and yet, because of their flagrant neglect of the ethical
aspects of the covenant, YHWH would take them into exile. Jerusalem would be like Samaria (cf. Micah 1:6)! This is the first prophetic mention of the fall
of Jerusalem ("plowed as a field") and the temple (i.e. overgrown with vegetation, literally "a high place of a forest"). This is theologically parallel to Isaiah 5.
This verse is quoted in Jer. 26:18 during Jeremiah's trial for false prediction.

I am sure that Micah was discredited in 701 B.C. when this did not occur (i.e. Sennacherib's army destroyed by YHWH,
cf. 2 Kgs. 19:35-37), however, the prophet was vindicated in 586 B.C. when this prophecy was literally fulfilled under the siege of Nebuchadnezzar II
of Babylon. F. F. Bruce, Answers to Questions, asserts that the king (i.e. Hezekiah, cf. Micah 1:1) and people of Judah responded to Micah's message and,
therefore, God relented of His judgment (p. 36). Hezekiah's repentance is recorded in 2 Kgs. 20:1-7.

▣ "on account of you" They (the political and religious leaders) were not only going to experience the judgment of YHWH (like the wealthy exploiters),
their activities were the reason for the judgment of God!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us
must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What was the essence of the false prophets' message in Micah 2:6-11?

- Why is Micah 2:12-13 such a radical break from the context?

- How does one tell the difference between a false prophet and a true prophet?

- How can God promise to always have a man on the Davidic throne
(2 Samuel 7), and yet predict the total destruction of Jerusalem and the monarchy?
